corrections.text: The article's opening sentence quotes TechCrunch as saying "all third-party browsers on iOS must use Apple's WebKit engine." TechCrunch's January 26, 2024 article does not contain that sentence; it actually says "Currently Apple mandates third party browsers use WebKit, the same browser engine that underpins its own Safari browser." The underlying fact is accurate, but the quotation marks incorrectly presented a paraphrase as a verbatim quote.

The article states that Apple requires "any alternative engine" to "ship an updated app within fifteen calendar days of a new engine version." Apple's published terms scope that fifteen-day requirement specifically to the Embedded Browser Engine Entitlement (used for in-app browsing), not to the Web Browser Engine Entitlement that a standalone browser app would use. The 90%/80% test-suite thresholds and the 30-day active-exploit mitigation window cited in the same sentence do apply to both entitlement types, as stated.
